entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Cherarkey K Samson
entries.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, we have agreed that COVID-19 is a serious pandemic and the President issued protocols. He was emphatic that the curfew time is 9.00 p.m. He said that no one should be exempted. In fact, he said a mheshimiwa . Therefore, we must follow the health protocols. We cannot be leaders who are breaking the rules. What example will we be showing the country? The curfew starts at 9.00 p.m. and we must go home. That is my concern.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Several Senators consulted loudly)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Order, Hon. Senators! There are 15 Members who want to contribute to this Motion and it is their right. I also have six Members who have points of order. This is a House of order. Tomorrow is another day. I do not want us to abuse the process of this House. Let us respect the process of the House and let us allow those who have points of order to raise them. It is not fair for you give your point of order then expect us to skip another Member. I proposed the question and the first Member who wanted to contribute to the Motion was interrupted. Nobody has contributed to the Motion other than the Mover and the Seconder. I want to have a feel of the points of orders.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Stewart Mwachiru Shadrack Madzayo
entries.text: Ahsante sana, Bi Naibu Spika. Sisi ni watumishi wa kaunti zetu na tuko hapa kufanya kazi. Sisi ni essential workers . Hii ni hoja ya nidhamu. Kwa hivyo, ni vyema uongeze wakati ndiposa tuweze kujadili Hoja hii ambayo ni muhimu kwa maisha ya Wakenya.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Point taken. Sen. Murkomen, you were on a point of order.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, the issue before you is very simple. There was a Motion that was proposed by Sen. Khaniri and it was passed by this House. It was passed that the Senate will only adjourn if the business in the Order Paper is completed. Anyone desirous of cutting the debate time should use the Standing Orders. Anyone questioning the legal framework that governs our stay here should know that we are governed by the Standing Orders. Let us not be coarse just because we are losing a debate. Let us not cut short the procedures of this House. That is because you are either on this side today, and the other side tomorrow. We should stick to the Standing Orders.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Sen. Murkomen, do not go that direction.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Susan Wakarura Kihika
entries.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, I am surprised that the Senators are talking of how long our Standing Orders allows us to stay here yet they are all aware that the President of the Republic of Kenya, President Uhuru Kenyatta, directed that not even the waheshimiwa are above the law. The Senate should adjourn at 9.00 p.m. Tomorrow is another day.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: The last point of order is from Sen. Halake, and then I will rule.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Abshiro Soka Halake
entries.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, thank you very much. I do not know what the debate is about because if lateness is what we are talking about, we are already late. We are already late. This House should conclude on what it is supposed to be doing today. The issue has been overtaken by events, and, therefore, let us continue. Do not run away because you are sensing defeat.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Hon, Senators, I am going to make a ruling. I thought we had become very orderly and serious. The country is watching.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. Omogeni and Sen. M. Kajwang' stood up in their places)

entries.label: speech
entries.text: Order, Senators Omogeni and M. Kajwang'. Can you take your seats? Hon. Senators, this is a discussion that has been with us for a very long time. As a Member said, this discussion has come before us six times and it has been thrown out. You cannot blame anybody expect the Senators themselves. We need to blame ourselves first instead of creating a crisis out of a situation that we could have saved. Hon. Senators, I want to appeal to you. The number of Senators who want to contribute to this Motion is 12. We allowed three hours for the first amendment that we had. We were extremely fair to Sen. Kang'ata's amendment. It would be extremely unfair not to give the amendment by Sen. Sakaja the right time.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Applause)

entries.label: speech
entries.text: We need another three hours. That is the first point. I have ignored the six points of order. Are we going to be the Senate that does not obey the laws of the land?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Senators
entries.text: No way!

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Order, Senators! Hon. Senators, allow me to make the ruling.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Senators
entries.text: Put the question!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Why are you telling me to put the question even before I make the ruling? The only Member who almost started contributing was interrupted by points of order. He was not even able to contribute. We do not even know who is supporting and who is not. Hon. Senators, the importance of debate is to sway the minds of people who are on the borderline.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Senators
entries.text: Correct! Kabisa!

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Applause)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: Hon. Senators, I will tell you this while standing here that we cannot purport to be fair to Sen. Sakaja's Motion when we gave Sen. Kang'ata three hours and we are giving Sen. Sakaja one minute.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Senators
entries.text: He has not complained!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text: This Motion is in the House. So, it is not for him to complain or not; it is us because it is now our property.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: heading
entries.text: ADJOURNMENT

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Sen. (Prof.) Kamar)
entries.text:
Hon. Senators, going by what Sen. Kihika and a few others have said, it is now 9.05 p.m. It is now time for interruption of the business of the House. Therefore, the Senate stands adjourned until, Tuesday, 4th August, 2020, at 2.30 p.m.

The Senate rose at 9.06 p.m.
